newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOL signs 5 bln Florint credit line, gas deal.
newsitem.headline: MOL signs 5 bln Florint credit line, gas deal.

text.p: Hungarian oil and gas firm MOL Rt said on Thursday it signed a five billion forints credit line agreement with a bank consortium for five years of maturity with an interest rate of BUBOR plus 17.5 basis points.
BUBOR stands for Budapest Interbank Offered Rates, which are set for one-, three- and six-month by the National Bank of Hungary daily.

The loan, provided by ABN AMRO Bank (Magyarorszag Rt), ING Bank Rt and Raiffeisen Unicbank Rt, will be used to refinance existing forint loans by exploiting favourable market conditions in the Hungarian forint market, MOL said in a statement.
"Following the very successful deals on the international syndicated loan markets MOL intends to play a prominent role on the local loan market as well," it said.
Separately, MOL said that it has signed a 20-year agreement with Csepel Power Plant Rt, wholly owned by PowerGen to supply natural gas for a 389 MW capacity power generator.
The generator is due to become operational by 2000 and it is expected to purchase some 500 million cubic meters natural gas annually.
